chapters.title: Job's first test
chapters.summary: Job is blameless and wealthy. Satan claims Job fears God only because he is blessed, and God allows him to be tested. Job loses his children and possessions, yet worships: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away.

chapters.title: Job's second test
chapters.summary: Satan is allowed to strike Job's body with painful sores. Job refuses to curse God. Three friends come and sit silently with him for seven days.

chapters.title: Job curses his birth
chapters.summary: Job breaks his silence and wishes he had never been born, asking why light is given to those in misery.

chapters.title: Eliphaz speaks
chapters.summary: Eliphaz suggests that the innocent do not perish, and describes a night vision asking whether any mortal can be righteous before God.

chapters.title: Eliphaz's advice
chapters.summary: Eliphaz urges Job to seek God and accept His discipline, promising that God wounds and also binds up.

chapters.title: Job answers Eliphaz
chapters.summary: Job says his grief outweighs the sand of the sea and his friends are like streams that dry up. He asks them to show him where he has gone wrong.

chapters.title: Job's despair
chapters.summary: Job describes life as hard service and his nights as restless. He asks God why He watches him so closely and will not leave him alone.

chapters.title: Bildad speaks
chapters.summary: Bildad insists God does not pervert justice and suggests Job's children died for their sins. If Job is pure, God will restore him.

chapters.title: Who can argue with God?
chapters.summary: Job agrees God is just, but asks how anyone can argue with the Creator. He longs for someone to mediate between them.

chapters.title: Job pleads with God
chapters.summary: Job speaks his bitterness and asks God why He made him with such care only to destroy him.

chapters.title: Zophar speaks
chapters.summary: Zophar rebukes Job's words and says God punishes less than Job deserves. He urges Job to put away sin and find hope.

chapters.title: Job's reply on wisdom
chapters.summary: Job mocks his friends' wisdom and says God holds all creatures in His hand, both wisdom and power.

chapters.title: Though He slay me
chapters.summary: Job wants to argue his case with God directly. Though He slay me, yet will I trust in Him. He calls his friends worthless physicians.

chapters.title: If a man dies
chapters.summary: Job reflects on how short and troubled human life is, like a flower that withers, and asks whether a man who dies will live again.

chapters.title: Eliphaz's second speech
chapters.summary: Eliphaz accuses Job of undermining reverence for God and describes the troubles of the wicked.

chapters.title: My witness is in heaven
chapters.summary: Job calls his friends miserable comforters and describes how God has broken him, yet says his witness is in heaven.

chapters.title: Where is my hope?
chapters.summary: Job feels his spirit is broken and his days are past, and asks where his hope could be.

chapters.title: Bildad's second speech
chapters.summary: Bildad describes the dark fate of the wicked, implying it is Job's.

chapters.title: I know my Redeemer lives
chapters.summary: Job feels abandoned by God, family and friends. Then he declares: I know that my redeemer liveth, and in my flesh I shall see God.

chapters.title: Zophar's second speech
chapters.summary: Zophar says the joy of the wicked is brief, and their gains will be taken from them.

chapters.title: Why do the wicked prosper?
chapters.summary: Job points out that the wicked often live long and prosper, which contradicts his friends' easy answers.

chapters.title: Eliphaz accuses Job
chapters.summary: Eliphaz accuses Job of specific sins against the poor and urges him to make peace with God.

chapters.title: Where is God?
chapters.summary: Job longs to find God and present his case. He cannot find Him, yet trusts: when He has tried me, I shall come forth as gold.

chapters.title: Injustice in the world
chapters.summary: Job describes the suffering of the poor and the crimes of the wicked, and asks why God seems not to act.

chapters.title: Bildad's short reply
chapters.summary: Bildad briefly says God is great and asks how any human can be pure before Him.

chapters.title: The edges of His ways
chapters.summary: Job describes God's power over the deep, the sky and the sea, and says these are only the edges of His ways.

chapters.title: Job holds to his integrity
chapters.summary: Job refuses to admit to wrongs he did not do and maintains his integrity until he dies.

chapters.title: Where is wisdom found?
chapters.summary: People mine the earth for treasure, but wisdom cannot be bought. God alone knows its place: the fear of the Lord is wisdom.

chapters.title: Job remembers better days
chapters.summary: Job recalls when God watched over him, when he was respected and helped the poor, the orphan and the widow.

chapters.title: Job's present misery
chapters.summary: Now Job is mocked by the young and in constant pain. He cries to God and receives no answer.

chapters.title: Job's final defense
chapters.summary: Job lists the sins he has not committed and swears his innocence, asking that God would answer him.

chapters.title: Elihu speaks
chapters.summary: A younger man, Elihu, angry at both Job and the friends, says wisdom comes from the Spirit of God, not only from age.

chapters.title: God speaks in many ways
chapters.summary: Elihu says God speaks through dreams and suffering to turn people from pride and bring them back.

chapters.title: God is just
chapters.summary: Elihu insists God cannot do wrong and accuses Job of speaking without knowledge.

chapters.title: Songs in the night
chapters.summary: Elihu says God is not affected by human sin or goodness, and asks why people do not seek God who gives songs in the night.

chapters.title: God's greatness
chapters.summary: Elihu says God uses affliction to teach, and that He is great beyond our understanding.

chapters.title: The storm approaches
chapters.summary: Elihu describes God's power in thunder, snow and rain, and calls Job to stand still and consider God's wonders.

chapters.title: God answers from the whirlwind
chapters.summary: God speaks to Job out of the whirlwind: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? He asks about the sea, the light and the stars.

chapters.title: The wild animals
chapters.summary: God asks Job about the wild goats, the donkey, the ox, the ostrich, the horse and the hawk, which He made and cares for.

chapters.title: Job responds
chapters.summary: Job lays his hand on his mouth. God asks whether Job would condemn Him to justify himself, and describes the mighty behemoth.

chapters.title: Leviathan
chapters.summary: God describes the fearsome Leviathan, which no human can tame, showing that everything under heaven belongs to Him.

chapters.title: Job's restoration
chapters.summary: Job repents: now my eye sees You. God rebukes the friends, Job prays for them, and God restores Job's fortunes twice over. Job dies old and full of days.
